Guards in tests/test_w1452_betweenness_determinism.py (11 tests): 5 fail against a behaviour-only revert that keeps the constant but strips seed=, the negative control is measured rather than hoped (unseeded sampling produced 12 distinct results in 12 runs, so the falsifier is not luck-dependent), a different-seed-gives-a-different-answer check rules out a draw-insensitive test graph, a boundary guard stops the fixture silently dropping below the sampling threshold, and an AST drift guard scans all of src/roam for any future betweenness_centrality call that passes k without seed. Migration consequence, stated rather than discovered later: the next roam index changes every stored betweenness value on any repository above 1000 symbols, so the first post-fix --baseline run shows a one-time step change in bottleneck values, band edges and population. That step is the fix landing, not architectural drift.
  • A typo in a fitness rule's type silently disabled that rule and left CI green. The dispatcher did checker = _CHECKERS.get(rule.get("type", "")); if checker is None: continue, and since rules_checked = len(rule_results), a rule with an unrecognised type vanished from BOTH the numerator and the denominator. The loader validated only that a rule was a dict, so nothing anywhere checked type against the four registered checkers. Measured with two eligible rules — one type: layer (the term the module docstring itself ADVERTISED) and one type: dependancy (a typo) — the command emitted rules_checked: 0, verdict all 0 fitness rule(s) pass, and exit 0. The user wrote two architectural rules, the tool enforced neither, and reported success. The W1051 comment three hundred lines below already stated the intent — warnings exist "so the agent doesn't see a green verdict that silently dropped half its rules" — but covered loader drops only, never dispatch drops. Fixed by failing closed AND disclosing, not one or the other: the load-bearing signal here is the exit code (roam fitness && echo "Architecture OK" ships in the --init template), so disclosure alone would leave the gate off while CI stayed green — the exact shape W1332 was written against. An unrecognised type now produces a rule-result row with status: "ERROR" and a difflib did-you-mean ('dependancy' → "Did you mean 'dependency'?"), rules_checked counts every rule the user wrote, _rule_counts returns (passed, failed, errored) under the invariant passed + failed + errored == len(rule_results), and _finish_fitness exits 1 on any errored rule ahead of every baseline branch. Two deliberate sub-calls, both pinned by tests: the ERROR row is kept OUT of all_violations, because a config typo is not a per-location finding and routing it there would let --write-baseline bless the typo into permanent silence; and the errored check precedes the baseline branches for the same reason. The structural half matters more than the fix: _resolve_checker() is now the single membership test that BOTH loader and dispatcher call, with _known_rule_types() reading tuple(sorted(_CHECKERS)), so registering a checker teaches both halves and no second hardcoded list can drift — proven behaviourally by tests that add AND delete a _CHECKERS key and assert the loader follows in both directions. The verdict string was also being re-derived from two copies of the same three-branch conditional in the text and JSON paths; both now call one _fitness_verdict(). The docstring's false "layer enforcement" claim — the trap that produces type: layer in the first place — was removed, along with the same false advertisement in the roam_fitness MCP tool description and docs/mcp-tools.md. Regression suite in tests/test_w1450_fitness_unknown_rule_type.py: 15 of 18 assertions confirmed failing against the pre-fix code. The 3 green in both states are the two negative controls (valid rules still checked, still PASS, still exit 0, no new envelope fields; and a mixed config still evaluating its valid rule) plus one direction of the drift test that is vacuously true pre-fix — its sister case fails there, which is the point.
  • roam preflight turned a fitness checker that CRASHED into Fitness: all 1 rules pass [OK]. The rule checker was wrapped in except (ImportError, re.error, sqlite3.DatabaseError): violations = [], and status was then derived as PASS if not violations else FAIL — so a rule whose checker raised produced an empty violation list, which is also exactly what a genuinely clean rule produces. The rule stayed counted in rules_checked, so the text renderer reported a full pass and _fitness_severity(0) returned OK. The zero-rule case was disclosed ("no rules configured"); the exception case was not, making it a half-fix. Proven by divergence rather than by inspection: given a rule with the malformed pattern handle_([, roam fitness exits 1 with unterminated character set at position 8 — loud and fail-closed — while roam preflight exited 0 with status: PASS, violations: 0, severity: OK, byte-identical to a healthy-rule control run. Same rule file, same checker, opposite verdicts; that disagreement is what proves it was fail-open rather than a deliberate choice. The except is retained — one broken rule must not take the other N-1 down — but a caught exception now yields status: "ERROR" with violations: None rather than 0, mirroring db-check's count: None, because a floored zero reads as "ran, measured nothing" while None says no measurement happened. New rules_evaluated / rules_errored / errored_rules fields report the shortfall, rules_checked deliberately keeps meaning rules attempted so it still agrees with len(rule_details), and severity is floored off OK to WARNING when any rule errors — otherwise an all-ERROR section rolled into _overall_risk as clean. Markers reach summary.warnings_out and flip partial_success through the existing plumbing, and preflight's text mode gained echo_text_warnings (stderr, so stdout stays byte-identical) since it previously disclosed nothing at all. One structural fix beyond the defect: four hand-rolled three-bucket warning concatenations were replaced by a single _all_warnings_out(), so a newly added bucket can no longer reach three call sites and silently miss the fourth — which is how a disclosure channel quietly loses a branch. Regression suite in tests/test_w1449_preflight_checker_exception.py: 13 of 15 assertions confirmed failing against the pre-fix code, including an AST guard that names the flooring line. The 2 passing in both states are the divergence pin and a load-bearing negative control asserting byte-equality of the healthy-rule text Fitness: all 1 rules pass [OK] — without it, a "fix" that simply failed everything would have scored green.
  • roam health reported two SQL LIMIT constants as if they were populations, and issue_count was literally their sum. The god-component and bottleneck sections render a top-N list, but the caps were inline literals passed straight to LIMIT ?, so once saturated the returned list length was indistinguishable from a measured count. Measured on this repository: summary.god_components: 50 against a true population of 553, bottlenecks: 15 against 3019, and issue_count: 65 — exactly 50 + 15 — all published with summary.partial_success: false and an empty preserved_list_truncations, i.e. an explicit claim of completeness. The envelope contradicted itself inside one document, printing bottleneck_thresholds.population: 3019 beside a bottleneck count of 15. Neither threshold is reachable in practice, so this is not a quirk of one repository: the 50th-ranked symbol here has degree 142 against a threshold of 20, and betweenness is unnormalised (raw shortest-path counts) so the 15th-ranked value is ~1.5e7 against a threshold of 0.5 — the cap, never the threshold, is what stops the cursor. Nothing upstream could have caught it, because output.formatter records only the truncations it performs and this one happens in SQL, beneath that layer; the disclosure was therefore made in good faith. The caps are now named constants, the god section publishes a measured god_component_thresholds.population counted against the same > min_degree predicate its items are filtered on (the bottleneck section already published its population but never said the list was capped, so both now carry list_limit too), and a saturated list raises partial_success with a marker naming the true population. Text mode says "top 50 of 553 god components" rather than "50 god components". Disclosure requires BOTH cursor saturation AND a population exceeding the cap — not saturation alone: TOP_BY_DEGREE/TOP_BY_BETWEENNESS carry no WHERE clause, so on any project with at least limit indexed symbols they return a full list even when nothing clears the qualifying threshold, and a full list is not a truncated one. That distinction was found by a negative control in the new suite firing against the first version of this fix, which would otherwise have shipped a false truncation claim on every small clean project. Guards in tests/test_w1448_health_list_cap_disclosure.py seed a population larger than the caps rather than relying on this repository staying large, and include a control asserting the lists are still capped (so "disclose" cannot degrade into "return everything") and one asserting silence on an unsaturated project. Deliberately NOT changed, and recorded rather than quietly folded in: issue_count and the health score still derive from the capped, classified sample. Those signals count actionable items — a per-item classification that only ever ran on the fetched rows — so substituting a raw population would change what the metric means rather than uncap it, and the score's scales were themselves tuned on the now-falsified premise (a code comment reads "this repo had 50 god components total"; 50 was the LIMIT). Correcting those needs classification over the full population plus a stated re-tune, tracked separately.
  • roam verdict — the gate itself — returned exit 0 and all_required_passed on a bundle that recorded no passing check, because satisfaction was written as a denylist. The previous fix in this area (W1441) closed the status-less-record fail-open inside proof_bundle._extract_executed_checks and expressed the rule downstream as status != "unverified". A denylist only refuses the one value it was taught to distrust, so every other value satisfied a required check. Measured against the shipped 13.10.0 binary with a contract requiring pytest -q, all four of these returned exit 0 / pass / all_required_passed: a record with status "skipped", a record with no status field at all — the exact shape W1441's own commit message names — a record with status "Unverified", where capitalisation alone defeated the comparison, and a record with status null. Two things made it invisible. First, proof_bundle.validate_v1 does reject those shapes against the closed CHECK_STATUSES enum, but cmd_verdict never calls it, so two validators in the same codebase disagreed about the same bundle and nothing compared them. Second, the CLI read body["tests_run"] raw rather than through the normaliser build_proof_bundle uses, so W1441's hardening sat one layer below the entry point a caller actually invokes. The fix inverts the direction rather than extending the list of distrusted values: satisfaction is now an allowlist on "pass", which fails closed on statuses nobody has invented yet — something a denylist cannot do by construction. A record carrying a status outside the enum no longer reports as "not run" but gets its own blocker code, required_check_status_invalid, carrying the offending value, since "you never ran this" and "you ran it and recorded no outcome" call for different actions from the agent reading the reason. fail/error are deliberately excluded from the new blocker so the failure loop keeps reporting them precisely instead of one defect surfacing as two unrelated reasons, and the legacy tests_run path now shares the one normaliser so the two halves cannot drift apart again. Regression suite in tests/test_w1447_verdict_status_allowlist.py: 13 of its 18 assertions were confirmed failing against the pre-fix code, and the 5 that pass in both states are the negative controls — a genuinely passing check must still pass, a failing one must still be reported as failed rather than as missing, unverified must keep its more specific code, and every member of CHECK_STATUSES must agree with the allowlist so the schema enum and the gate cannot diverge again. Those controls are load-bearing: without them, a "fix" that blocked unconditionally would have made the suite green. Known limit, unchanged and stated rather than quietly patched: a bundle carrying no verification_contract at all still returns pass, because an empty required-set is vacuously satisfied. That is the already-disclosed "the gate reads a contract from the bundle the agent authors" limit, and closing it is not a matter of tightening this predicate — it requires an authority outside the agent's write boundary to supply the contract, which is a separate, deliberately open design question.
  • roam taint re-scanned the entire corpus once per rule, per file, per name — 292,221 whole-file regex passes of which 98.1% could not match, making it 94% of the reachability-triage service report. _scan_hits compiled a boundary-anchored pattern for every candidate name and ran finditer over the whole masked file text, three times per (rule, file) — once each for sources, sinks and sanitizers. The cost was the corpus length multiplied by every name any Python rule declares, and almost all of it bought nothing: the overwhelming majority of those scans traversed a file that does not contain the name anywhere. The fix is a single substring pre-check, and it is sound for a reason worth stating precisely — _dotted_name_pattern compiles to (?<!\w) + re.escape(name) + (?!\w), which only ADDS boundary lookarounds and never widens what can match, so a literal occurrence of the name is a strict necessary condition for a match and name not in masked_text cannot skip a hit the regex would have found. Measured on this repository (4,898 files / 44,412 symbols, warm index): taint 87.4s → 15.6s, service-report --type reachability-triage 96.4s → 28.1s, with 286,659 of the 292,221 scans eliminated and the emitted payload byte-identical outside volatile _meta timestamps. Because the argument, not the arithmetic, is what makes this safe, tests/test_w1446_taint_scan_prefilter.py proves equivalence by differential execution against an oracle that reimplements the pre-fix loop, and separately pins the two regex properties the pre-check depends on: that the escaped literal still appears in the compiled pattern, and that the pattern is not case-insensitive. If anyone later loosens _dotted_name_pattern, the necessary-condition argument breaks and the scanner starts silently missing taint findings — a failure with no symptom — so those guards fail loudly instead. Found by measuring a dogfood defect (M8) that had been carried as an unmeasured estimate since 2026-07-15; every specific in the original triage was wrong. due-diligence was recorded at "~130s" and is 87.5s, so it was never the headline offender; reachability-triage was recorded at "~41s" and had regressed to 96.4s, unnoticed because M8 was pinned only as pytest.mark.slow with a 300s ceiling and no perf assertion; and the guessed root cause (dead/clones/complexity fan-out) was wrong, complexity being 0.42s of it. The registry entry has been rewritten with measured numbers. One measured cost is deliberately left open and recorded rather than fixed: due-diligence extracts only 1.38x from its 3 workers (120.5s serial against 87.5s wall, ideal makespan ~47.5s) because three concurrent CLI children each re-open a 97MB index.db — raising the worker cap would add contention over the same file rather than remove it.
  • Every mined import law fired backwards on every src/-layout project: the conventional internal import was flagged, and the one spelling that cannot import at runtime was cleared. The miner bucketed file paths read from the index (src/roam/db/connection.py → src/roam) while the checker bucketed module paths read from a diff (from roam.db.connection import open_db → roam/db). Under a src layout those two namespaces never intersect, so the polarity inverted: from roam.db.connection import open_db — what every test in this repo writes — was reported as a layering violation, while from src.roam.db.connection import open_db, naming a package that does not exist and fails at import, passed clean. Measured on this repository over the trailing 29 non-merge commits: 47 violations raised, 0 of them true — conventional from roam.<pkg> import <name> lines, the repo's own mandated test-root helper import, one stdlib module absent from a hand-rolled allowlist, and one line of prose inside a docstring that the diff parser read as an import. After the fix, the same 29 commits raise 1, and that one is factually correct: a test that really does import across the boundary its law describes. The existing coverage missed all of this because its fixture diff imports from src.forbidden.module import bad_helper, a spelling that includes the source root and that no src-layout project ever writes. Both halves now bucket through one new module, roam.laws.namespace, which re-expresses a file path in the namespace an import statement can actually name. Source roots are detected from repo layout rather than special-cased on the name src: a directory that holds packages, holds no loose modules of its own, and is not itself importable — so lib/, python/ and a monorepo's packages/app/src fall out of the same rule, and a repo that declares no source root (any flat layout, any non-Python tree) is bucketed exactly as before and does not move. Three further false-positive sources in the same checker were closed while the measurement was open: the stdlib allowlist became sys.stdlib_module_names, so the missing statistics cannot recur with the next module anyone adopts; "is this import ours?" is now asked of the checkout — does a directory or module of that name exist at the repo root or under a source root — instead of of a hand-maintained list of third-party names; and relative imports are resolved against the importing file's own directory, since from .helpers import x names a sibling, not a top-level package helpers. A fourth, found while verifying the first: lstrip("./") strips characters, so .github/scripts/gate.py bucketed as github/scripts and the law mined from that directory named a directory that does not exist. The two xfail(strict=True) tests shipped in tests/test_w1439_laws_import_law_src_layout.py flipped to XPASS on the fix and are now ordinary assertions; the mechanism, the source-root rule, and each false-positive class are pinned in tests/test_w1440_laws_namespace_contract.py, including an end-to-end mine-then-check round trip over a synthetic src-layout project that is not this repository. Every new assertion was run against a deliberately broken version of the property it protects and confirmed to fail there.
  • Four of the eleven laws this repository mined could never have fired, and were mined anyway. added_symbols() labels every declaration it recognises as function or class, so the mined constant, method, property and variable naming laws matched nothing on every diff — a diff flagrantly violating all four reported clean. Mining stopped for kinds the checker cannot observe, rather than teaching the checker to observe them: constant is the case that settles it, because the Python indexer classifies a symbol as a constant iff its name is upper-case, which makes "constants must be UPPER_SNAKE" true by construction and unfalsifiable no matter how good the checker gets; method is already covered by snake_case_functions, since the diff regex labels every def a function; and property and variable need decorator and scope tracking that a regex over added lines cannot honestly do. The skip is not a hardcoded list — the miner reads roam.laws.checker.CHECKABLE_SYMBOL_KINDS and declines to mine anything outside it, so widening the checker re-enables the corresponding laws automatically and the two halves cannot drift apart again. The dropped kinds are disclosed in the laws mine envelope as skipped_naming_kinds with a reason, so a shorter law list arrives with an explanation rather than as silent attrition. A guard test fails if CHECKABLE_SYMBOL_KINDS is ever widened past what added_symbols() actually emits, which is the exact shape of the defect being removed.
  • roam cycle-break printed nothing at all on a corpus with no symbols indexed, and roam clusters reported "no clusters detected" for it. The empty-corpus branch in cycle-break had a if json_mode: with no else — text mode produced zero bytes of output and exit 0, which a caller reads as "there are no cycles to break". clusters printed the same verdict for an unbuilt index as for a genuinely well-modularised repository, while its JSON envelope carried state: empty_corpus. Both now disclose through the shared formatter.echo_text_empty_corpus() helper, and cycle-break gained the missing verdict line. Measured on a real 0-symbol index; the populated-fixture control stays silent. Reviewed the other three empty_corpus_state baseline entries in the same pass — cycles, alerts and debt already name the empty corpus in their text verdict, so they are instrument false positives and were left alone rather than double-disclosed. Ratchet baseline 54 → 52.
  • Thirteen more W1331 disclosure asymmetries closed, this time on the commands a human runs to answer "is this safe?". roam adversarial is the sharpest: with its severity classifier raising, the command printed VERDICT: No architectural challenges found -- changes look clean while the JSON envelope named the failure — a review command certifying clean off a scorer that never ran. roam doctor skips any check helper that raises, so a raising check produced no PASS line, no FAIL line, and no failed_checks entry: the health report a user reads to answer "is my install broken?" simply omitted it and the verdict counted one fewer check. roam vuln-reach reported 0 reachable vulnerabilities after the symbol graph failed to build. roam health rendered a failed graph build as Tangle: 0.0% (0/44309 symbols in cycles) — the best possible score — with no note. roam cga verify printed see warnings_out in its error list while never printing warnings_out. roam sbom on this repository already discloses a real, un-injected truncation (reachability_scan_truncated: file cap reached; unimported/phantom verdicts may under-report) that only the JSON envelope carried. Also fixed: audit-trail-verify, evidence-doctor, flag-dead (an unreadable --config silently disabled known-stale matching), and a scope bug found while proving the cga fix — the W489-A qualified_only lint bucket was built inside the if json_mode: branch, so the text tail could not have disclosed it even in principle. Same template as the previous entry: markers to STDERR via formatter.echo_text_warnings(), stdout byte-identical.
  • failed_checks demoted from the W1331 gated vocabulary to the measured-only set, and four buckets renamed to the codebase's own convention. Both live failed_checks instances were run and found to disclose in every branch, just not under that name: adversarial appends the errored-check list to the VERDICT line verbatim, and doctor renders one [WARN]/[FAIL] row per entry plus a count. Gating an envelope KEY NAME there measured spelling, not disclosure — the same reasoning that already exempts partial_success. Separately, rules, check-rules and flag-dead were flagged while their text branches already printed the warnings; their buckets were named _rules_warnings / deduped_warnings / _known_stale_warnings, outside the *_warnings_out convention the instrument matches on, so the disclosure was invisible to the scan. Renamed rather than re-disclosed. The ratchet baseline drops 67 → 54.
  • The anti-leak gates reported clean over content they had never correctly read: an empty file inventory and any UTF-16 file. Two defect shapes, both proven by end-to-end reproduction against the real scanners before anything was changed, both silent — neither produced a diagnostic distinguishing "found nothing" from "read nothing". First, the whole-tree scanners shape their verdict as "hits among the enumerated tracked files" and never checked that the enumeration produced anything. git ls-files honours GIT_INDEX_FILE/GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE; pointed at another index it prints nothing and exits 0, and both scripts/scan_internal_language.py --all and the CI gate tests/test_no_internal_language.py then passed a tree holding a plainly-visible leak. That matters precisely because these run from .githooks/pre-commit and .githooks/pre-push, exactly where Git exports repository-local GIT_ controls — .githooks/pre-push already unsets them, so a push through the hook was defended while the CI invocation and any direct run were not. Both enumerations now strip GIT_ and fail closed on an empty answer, guarding the result rather than only its causes. The strip is deliberately NOT applied to --staged: git commit -- <pathspec> builds a temporary index and hands the hook its path in GIT_INDEX_FILE, and that index — not .git/index — is the authoritative statement of what the commit will contain. Second, decoding a UTF-16 file as UTF-8 reads it wrong rather than failing on it: every NUL padding byte is itself valid UTF-8, so nothing is dropped and an ASCII payload arrives NUL-interleaved, matching no pattern in the catalogue. The vector is concrete rather than theoretical on a Windows-developed repository — PowerShell's > redirect and Out-File emit UTF-16LE by default, so a credential captured to a file and accidentally staged lands as tracked content the gate cannot see. The catalogue module gains a single scan_bytes entry point applying the patterns across every text reading the bytes admit (BOM-directed, plus a NUL-stripped pass that is the only thing able to catch BOM-less UTF-16), deduplicated across readings; the hook CLI's working-tree, staged and pushed-history readers and the CI gate all route through it. scripts/secret_scan.py had the narrower version of the same gap — it honoured a BOM but could not see UTF-16 without one — and gains the same second reading. Verified across all 4,900 tracked files with no new findings and no runtime change, so the extra readings cost nothing in precision here. Regression suite in tests/test_leak_gate_blind_spots.py, every test confirmed failing against the pre-fix code.
  • Thirteen output-branch disclosure asymmetries closed: a degraded run that the JSON envelope reported honestly, while the SARIF a CI gate consumes and the text a human reads both said clean. Every one of the SARIF-blind entries in the W1331 ratchet is now gone. test-impact --sarif was the sharpest: with the default --limit, the cap-hit marker was assembled inside the if json_mode: branch alone, so a gate received the top-N slice of the impacted-test set with no truncation flag at all — measured on this repository, 2 of 972 reachable test files presented as the whole answer. roam algo folded its three warning buckets (malformed .roamignore-findings, malformed per-finding suppressions, unknown --only/--exclude names) together inside the JSON branch, so a suppression file that failed to parse disabled every suppression rule while SARIF and text reported an unannotated finding set. dead, clones, duplicates, fan, n1, over-fetch, orphan-imports, critique and dark-matter each floored a raised substrate call to an empty result and disclosed it only to --json; on the SARIF path that is an empty results array, which is exactly what a Code-Scanning gate reads as PASS. dead and clones additionally rendered the empty_corpus_state distinction — nothing indexed versus nothing found — in the JSON envelope only, so an unbuilt index printed the same all-clear as a clean repository. Each fix routes the existing bucket through formatter.echo_text_warnings() (and the new sibling formatter.echo_text_empty_corpus()) in the non-JSON tails: markers go to STDERR, so stdout stays byte-identical and no golden output moves. Every command was run before and after on a fixture where the signal genuinely fires, each with a clean control proving the disclosure stays silent on the happy path. The W1331 ratchet baseline drops 80 → 67 and its high-water mark with it.
  • Five commands absorbed a broken input into the value that means "fine", so a signal that could not be computed rendered as a signal that came back clean. One defect shape, five instances, each proven with a fixture where the signal genuinely should have fired and a positive control on the same fixture with healthy input. verify --checks tenant_scope: an unparseable .roam/verify.yaml made the guard loader return an empty tuple, which is also what the deliberate "disable this detector" configuration returns — the detector switched itself off on a typo, dropping both the WARN finding and its agent_contract.risks entry with no disclosure anywhere. The loader now returns the guards and an error channel, and the two empty states are no longer confusable. verify --report: whole-repo target discovery returned an empty path list on any index-open failure, so a corrupt index scored 100/PASS with verification_complete: true and files_checked: 0 — while the non-report path on the identical database already failed loudly, so the two disagreed about the same file. Discovery failure now routes into the existing loud discovery-failure emitter (exit 5, verification_complete: false). db-check: three OperationalError paths were downgraded to severity: "ok", so dropping a core metrics table reported verdict OK, errors: 0, and --ci exited 0; a check that cannot run is now error or the new non-clean unsupported, its count is None rather than a measured zero, and the verdict gains INCOMPLETE. Found while proving it: the zero-symbols check queried a column name that does not exist, so it raised on every database, healthy or not, and was unconditionally masked — that check had never once run. roam algo detectors: twelve per-detector except sqlite3.Error: return [] handlers pre-empted the orchestrator, which already logs the failure and records it in failed_detectors; deleting them lets a detector whose query fails be reported as failed instead of as finding nothing. service-report reachability-triage: three security counters in the executive summary carried a 0 default while their own sibling sections rendered an em-dash for the same absent field, so a failed component printed "Taint flows: 0" in one section and "—" in another. Regression suite in tests/test_w1332_uncomputable_signal_floor.py, every test paired with a negative control so a fix that merely makes everything loud cannot pass, plus a structural guard that fails if the swallow-into-empty-list handler is reintroduced in the detector catalog.
  • roam pr-prep <range> scored the working tree instead of the range, and could clear a critical change set as safe. pr-prep bundles diff + critique + pr-risk into one ready_to_open envelope. The diff sub-invocation forwarded the positional commit_range; the pr-risk one only ever forwarded --staged, so the two sections of a single envelope described different change sets. On a clean tree the un-scoped pr-risk resolves to no-changes and scores 0 — measured on roam's own repository, pr-risk HEAD~20..HEAD returns 79/100, "Critical risk … significant blast radius" (driver: blast_pct) while the bare call pr-prep actually made returns no-changes, 0. ready_to_open is computed off exactly that score, so this was a false-clean rather than a cosmetic mismatch. Pre-existing since v12.17. The fix mirrors diff's precedence (an explicit range wins over --staged); the regression tests assert at the argv boundary where the defect lived, rather than on a risk score, so they do not become a tuning tripwire — including one that requires diff and pr-risk to be scoped identically, since a reader takes two sections of one envelope as two views of one thing.
  • The publish workflow's GitHub Release job had never once executed end to end, and hid four independent defects behind each other. PyPI publication and evidence signing were green throughout; every failure was downstream of them, which is why the gap survived. In order of discovery: actions/download-artifact resolving by artifact-ids nests the payload under a directory named after the artifact, so four path: values pointed one level above the files their consumers opened; cosign sign-blob --output-certificate writes base64-encoded PEM, which cosign verify-blob decodes transparently but openssl x509 cannot read — the sibling .sig was already decoded in the same loop and the certificate never was; GET /releases/tags/{tag} does not resolve draft releases (a draft carries no tag ref yet, hence its untagged-* URL), so the state fetch returned 404 again immediately after creating the draft and the tag assertion ran against the stale 404 body, making the whole create → upload → publish branch unreachable; and download_release_assets opened with mkdir -m 0700 on a directory every caller had already created with mktemp -d, which under set -e killed the job one step after the assets had been uploaded. Each fix was verified against the real artifacts the previous failure left behind rather than by re-running and hoping: the evidence certificates verify Verified OK for both subjects from the downloaded bytes, and all six assets download by tag from a draft release. The certificate decode falls back to the file as-is, so a cosign that emits bare PEM keeps verifying; more than one draft for a tag is now a hard error rather than a guess.

Changed

  • The .roam/responses/ side-car store is now bounded, indexed, and discloses its own truncation. It was an unbounded write-only cache — measured at 29,456 JSON files / 762,725,362 bytes on one real store — with no prune, evict, retention or cap anywhere in the write path, and both readers (roam next and roam pr-bundle) called iterdir() + stat() across every file on every invocation to consume a single newest envelope. roam next is meant to be fast and was O(n) in a corpus that only grows; the read path measured 988 ms -> ~308 ms steady state. Two things changed that a consumer can observe. (a) A new on-disk artifact, .roam/response-index.sqlite3, which both readers now consult instead of walking the store; it is a rebuildable cache, not a source of truth. (b) A 256 KB cap on the persisted payload (_DEFAULT_RESPONSE_STORE_MAX_BYTES in src/roam/output/formatter.py, overridable via ROAM_RESPONSE_STORE_MAX_BYTES), applied because the bytes live in a handful of commands rather than in the file count — dead alone was 40% of all bytes in 0.5% of the files, and the cap reclaims 63.4% of the corpus across 0.99% of it. Truncation is never silent: it goes through budget_truncate_json, preserves the envelope and contract blocks, and stamps summary.response_store ({payload_truncated, max_bytes, original_bytes, stored_bytes}) plus the canonical partial-success disclosure. The command's own stdout envelope is unchanged — only the persisted side-car copy is capped, and the write path runs at all only when ROAM_RUN_ID is set or .roam/pr-bundles/ holds a .json. A consumer that reads .roam/responses/ directly and does not check summary.response_store can now receive a truncated payload where it previously received the whole one; that is the one behaviour to plan against.
  • Author identity is reconciled through a .mailmap instead of a history rewrite. Six identities across the history are one person, accumulated across machines and git configs; git shortlog, git blame, git log --use-mailmap and GitHub's contributor graph now agree on 2,028 commits without touching published history. Outside contributors and the three automation identities are deliberately left distinct — two of them share an address with a human identity, so the entries touching that address match on name as well as email, since an email-only rule would have swallowed them.

[13.10.0] — 2026-07-28

Added

  • roam savings + roam savings-backfill — proof-oriented Procedure Foundry telemetry — prompt compilation and Claude Stop hooks now share a per-turn episode_id, preserving compile identity, terminal outcome, verification state, changed-file count, and privacy-preserving diff identity in an append-only local ledger. savings materializes the ledger into SQLite and withholds savings claims until known-answer canaries, telemetry integrity, hook-version coverage, compile joins, terminal coverage, and explicit verification-health coverage pass. savings-backfill mines local Claude/Codex transcripts into a replaceable historical discovery snapshot: raw prompts, responses, paths, shell values, and tool arguments are excluded, while keyed intent fingerprints plus sanitized shell templates/sequences/n-grams retain repeated workflow structure. Historical frequency can nominate automation experiments but can never satisfy the prospective evidence gate.
  • roam --json savings --aggregate — the platform savings privacy boundary — emits a versioned, closed, aggregate-only contract with producer-authored state and verdict labels. The envelope excludes session, turn, episode, prompt, response, path, command, and generic agent-contract fields, so Prakteon can ingest readiness and outcome coverage without receiving local transcript content or per-episode identifiers.
  • Complete-evidence roam verify autofire contract — changed-scope discovery now covers staged, unstaged, untracked, renamed, deleted, and unborn-HEAD worktrees; refreshes stale index targets; and reports explicit completeness, discovery, timeout, parsing, unavailable-check, and partial-success state. Any incomplete non-advisory check or malformed test protocol blocks the gate instead of producing a false pass. Claude Stop hooks consume the strict envelope, refuse edited-turn completion without complete evidence, and prohibit automatic fixes from changing policy, baselines, scopes, or suppressions.
  • Default-on execution-mode enforcement — CLI and MCP write surfaces fail closed when policy loading or mode resolution fails, while read-only diagnostics retain a conservative fallback. Emergency overrides are explicit, audited, and reflected in MCP receipts; verify and replay-capable sibling-patch operations carry truthful side-effect classifications.
  • Hardened local telemetry and replay containment — compile telemetry is explicit opt-in, closed-schema, size/time bounded, and owner-only from byte zero. Raw prompts, raw prompt hashes, session/turn identifiers, and compiler fingerprints are excluded; an optional opaque episode join key and keyed repo-local task fingerprint preserve outcome joins and repeat detection without exposing prompt text. The derived savings database is rebuilt as an exact owner-only projection with no on-disk SQLite journal, so bounded-source retention also removes stale rows. Sibling-patch replay uses literal argv, a scrubbed environment, isolated HOME/TMP roots, bounded process-tree termination, and explicitly discloses that this is process containment rather than a kernel sandbox.
  • Digest-bound release provenance — the publish workflow builds wheel and sdist once, validates tag/package identity, binds both artifacts and the CycloneDX SBOM into a closed manifest, transfers immutable artifacts between privilege boundaries, uses PyPI Trusted Publishing, and verifies published PEP 740 provenance before attaching release evidence.
  • Private cross-project Procedure Foundry atlas — transcript backfill v6 derives closed intent archetypes, action phases, exact/near-intent clusters, result-size buckets, time-to-action, directly observed friction counters (code slicing, shell replay, verification retry, search/inspect cycles, post-edit context recovery, structured-output post-processing, help lookup, and failure replay), per-sanitized-template attempts/failures/no-results/retries/result-volume aggregates, and closed failure-reason labels. Executables, subcommands, flags, compile procedures, artifact labels, prefetched facts, and probe names now cross persistence only through closed vocabularies; unsupported identifiers collapse to other. Search exit code 1 is classified as no_results, not a tool failure. Failure text is classified transiently and discarded. Rankings disclose likely scripted/eval contamination separately and use an organic-support estimate; associated time/tokens remain explicitly non-causal.
  • Universal repeatable --select EXPR JSON projection — every command can now project its completed envelope with the dependency-free subset .field, .field.nested, [N], and [START:END] (for example roam complexity --select '.symbols[:5]'). Projection happens only at final serialization, after the complete envelope is available to evidence sidecars, and --select implies --json.
  • roam grep bounded context packets — -C/--context now returns live match windows and --whole-symbol returns deduplicated enclosing-symbol packets, bounded by --max-packets and --max-packet-lines. Every match links to its packet; packet truncation, unreadable source, unindexed symbols, and stale indexed spans are explicit. A stale whole-symbol span safely falls back to a live match window instead of showing the wrong function.
  • Capability intervention contracts and transition-test atlas — @roam_capability(displaces=(...)) declares which repeated-work families a command is designed to replace. Procedure Foundry AST-reads these hypotheses without importing the lazy command tree and emits intervention_mappings plus prospective transition tests. Declarations do not discount historical research priority: effectiveness remains unmeasured until explicit exposure, joined terminal outcomes, transition reduction, and outcome non-inferiority pass. The savings ledger now understands paired pre-delivery intervention_assignment and terminal intervention_observation events, session-clustered intent-to-treat assignment, contamination disclosure, delivery/adoption coverage, and a pre-registered promotion contract with power analysis, confidence intervals, effect-size floors, and outcome margins. Failure classes remain routing-ineligible until precision validation, and long no-edit candidates exclude unknown and passive-only research/review/planning/documentation intents.
  • roam at ranges and whole-symbol reads — roam at FILE:START-END replaces arbitrary sed windows, while roam at FILE:LINE --whole-symbol expands a search hit to its complete indexed function/class. --max-lines bounds output and reports truncation instead of silently dropping source.

Changed

  • The canonical pre-push gate now has an explicit bounded concurrency budget — full-suite pytest execution defaults to at most four workers, accepts a validated --workers 1..4 override, schedules by file with --dist loadfile, and forces native BLAS/OpenMP runtimes to one thread per worker. This prevents a large host—or poisoned inherited thread settings—from multiplying a bounded worker pool into destructive CPU, memory, and temp-directory contention while retaining deterministic parallel release coverage.
  • CI and the reusable action now resolve only reviewed dependency inputs — every source-checkout workflow environment is created from the exact uv.lock, release-only tools install from hash-locked wheelhouses, dependency auditing checks the installed locked environment without re-resolving it, and every third-party action is pinned by full commit SHA. The composite action validates all caller-controlled inputs before they reach shell or JavaScript, maps expressions through bounded environment variables, and requires an explicit opt-in before resolving the moving latest release.
  • Generated and copy-paste CI templates inherit the same fail-closed policy — GitHub, GitLab, Azure, Jenkins, CircleCI, and Bitbucket templates pin Roam 13.10.0; GitHub actions and supported runners are immutable, and container-based examples bind verified multi-architecture OCI digests. Required Guard, health, SLSA, and SARIF evidence fails closed; deliberately advisory scans preserve stdout, stderr, exit code, and an explicit state sidecar instead of using blanket || true or continue-on-error fallbacks.
  • Roam now owns its Claude hook maintenance authority end to end — canonical v11 hook bodies invoke maintenance-only verify and index operations with the explicit audited mode override themselves. Compile Code no longer rewrites installed Roam source or hook bodies, so one signed Roam artifact defines the hook behavior on every client.
  • Claude hook installation is a bounded control-plane update — settings and hook bodies are size-bounded, strict-JSON parsed, protected from duplicate keys, symlinks, junctions, hard links, and pre-install generation changes, then written through the canonical content-bound durable atomic writer with exact-interpreter commands. Create-only publication is native no-replace; existing state uses a final generation precheck and atomic last-writer-wins replacement without rolling back later writers. Unsafe paths stop without touching redirected content; recognized prior bodies remain healable from a closed digest registry.
  • Mixed MCP query/write tools are gated per invocation — catalog metadata continues to declare maximum callable effects, while the dispatch boundary binds the concrete call arguments. A query-only roam_fan call remains available in read_only; persist=True raises the call to safe_edit, emits a write receipt, and is blocked before execution at lower authority.
  • Generated constitution upgrades are provenance-bound — fresh constitution init files record a semantic digest for the generated mode snapshot. New defaults flow into runtime policy only while that snapshot remains unchanged; customized and legacy policies stay authoritative. roam constitution check now exposes migration state, while roam constitution upgrade previews per-mode changes and requires both explicit replacement acknowledgement and the preview's expected digest before replacing an unproven policy.

Security

  • roam taint --ci reported SAFE and exited 0 on a repository containing unambiguous SQL injection and OS command injection. taint_engine._symbols_matching only queries the symbols table for a rule's sources/sinks, and the Python indexer (python_lang.py) never materialises import-bound attribute chains (request.args) or external call targets (cursor.execute, os.system) as symbols rows — they are not local definitions, so relations.py::resolve_references has nothing to turn into an edge, and the forward-BFS pass had no nodes to connect. "0 findings" was therefore indistinguishable from "scanned and clean." Measured before/after on the shipped sqli rules-pack fixture (--rules-pack sqli matches 3 rules by substring: python-sqli, java-sqli, php-laravel-sqli): EXIT=0, "No taint findings across 3 rule(s)" → EXIT=5, 1 finding; the companion command-injection pack shows the same flip. run_taint gains an opt-in text-scan fallback (project_root kwarg, default None — byte-identical for every pre-existing direct call site) that anchors literal source/sink text occurrences to their enclosing function via already-indexed line ranges when a rule's DB-matched sources/sinks come back empty, plus a same-function co-occurrence pass for the "source and sink both in one handler" shape forward-BFS structurally can't express. Two precision guards keep it from over-firing: a parameterized-DB-call heuristic (execute(sql, params) stays clean, execute(sql + input) still flags) and dotted-names-only source matching (bare words like data/payload can't anchor to an unrelated local variable). summary.anchor_coverage (rules_evaluated / rules_zero_anchors) plus partial_success + warnings_out now make a rule that never resolved any anchor LOUD instead of folding into a clean verdict — closing W805-KKKK (language-mismatched rule packs silently reading as clean) as a side effect.
  • audit-trail-verify could not detect tampering with the most recent (tail) record, while its own help text claimed "tampering with any record ... breaks the chain." _verify_chain validates record N via record N+1's previous_record_hash back-link; there is no N+1 for the last record, so the tail — the most attacker-valuable record, since it holds the final verdict — could be edited in place with no detection. Every append now also stamps a sibling <trail>.head.json file holding the tail line's own SHA-256, cross-checked at verify time. Backward compatible by construction: a trail with no head file (foreign, hand-built, or written before this fix) gets no tail check — exactly the pre-fix behaviour — so existing trails do not fail closed on a field they never had. New summary.tail_protected discloses which case applied. A follow-up in the same wave closed a related silent gap: the head-file write itself had swallowed a bare OSError, which would have left a trail with no tail protection and no record of why; it is now routed through log_swallowed so the failure is visible at write time, not only at audit time. This remains a hash chain, not a keyed signature: an attacker who rewrites the trail and its head file together still leaves no trace. Separately, dogfood.yml's --no-audit-trail flag had disabled the very audit-trail and conformance checking the workflow advertises, silently printing conformance: None/100 on every CI run; the flag is dropped so each run reports the fresh trail's real Article 12 conformance score.
  • roam capsule --redact-paths leaked the directory tree it exists to hide. The flag correctly hashed symbols[].file and clusters[].label, but symbols[].signature and the warnings_out diagnostic accumulators were left untouched — a module-level string constant (FILE = "src/roam/commands/cmd_hooks.py") or an exception message naming a real path landed verbatim in free text. A whole-envelope scan on roam's own repository (43,958 symbols) found 266+ signatures leaking a real path, plus one exception-message path, after the originally-reported field-level leak had already been closed. Per-field redaction is exactly the kind of choke point a new field bypasses by omission, so it is replaced with a single text-level scrub (_scrub_text/_scrub_token) that tokenizes free text and hashes any token matching a real indexed path component wherever it appears — including a filename glued to a sentence-final period — applied to symbols[].signature and both warnings_out marker accumulators. --redact-paths help text now states the guarantee precisely: it hashes known indexed path components in file/label/signature/warnings_out; it does not invent redaction for an out-of-corpus path, and it does not hash symbol names themselves. A new whole-envelope regression test scans the full serialised output against a distinctive fixture tree rather than checking one field at a time, which is how this class of leak survived the original fix.
  • Three defects together made the vulnerability-surface report the opposite of the truth. vuln-map ingested reports without project_root, so the import scanner never ran and every genuinely-imported package showed "no match (not imported)" — measured 0/4 matched on the dogfood security fixture; the matched-count is now widened to include import-site evidence (not just resolved symbol ids, since third-party packages rarely have an indexed symbol), bringing it to 2/4. vulns --reachable-only post-filtered to reachable==1, which is always empty for import-site matches by design (they never seed a symbol id), and the verdict read that empty list as "table is empty / no scan available" — concealing 4 already-ingested CVEs; the pre-filter row count now carries through the verdict/summary so "no data" and "N rows, 0 reachable" are distinguishable in both text and JSON. Ingestion itself was a bare INSERT with no dedup, so re-importing the same report doubled the row count every time (4 → 8 on a second import, unbounded on further repeats), silently breaking any count-based CI gate; a NULL-safe UNIQUE index on (cve_id, package_name, source) plus an UPSERT that refreshes severity/title/match evidence on conflict makes re-import idempotent (stable at 4). source deliberately stays in the dedup key so two different scanners flagging the same CVE remain distinct findings rather than collapsing into one row, and a migration ledger pair was needed because a naive unique index would crash outright on a database that already holds duplicates from the pre-fix bug.

Fixed

  • MCP setup and read-only security evidence now fail closed at their final trust boundaries — JSON/TOML config publication is atomic, rejects linked primary and backup targets, and refuses a merge when the parsed config generation changed concurrently. The Codex adapter writes the current ~/.codex/config.toml STDIO contract without clobbering unrelated tables. Receipts bind repository/run provenance, caller identity, and a deep JSON-safe argument snapshot before execution, so tool-side environment or nested-input mutation cannot rewrite the audited invocation. Read-only marker output cannot spoof the boundary-owned prompt-injection metadata key.
  • Public setup guidance and discovery metadata now track the live runtime contract — generated preset counts include the always-registered expansion meta-tool, compliance exposes 14 tools, stale CI/help invocations are rejected by doc tests, redaction docs include prompt_injection_marker, and the MCP card discloses the optional bounded host-model summarization egress path.
  • Prerelease self-analysis no longer depends on an artifact that cannot exist yet — the composite action now has an explicit version: source mode that installs from its validated action checkout, requires matching non-editable PEP 610 provenance, and never falls back to PyPI. Roam's own PR self-analysis uses this mode, while downstream defaults remain pinned to the exact published release.
  • Interrupted indexing can no longer masquerade as a complete graph — every index run acquires a held OS lock and publishes the same PID, process-start identity (where available), and random generation in its lock and durably synced in_progress marker before the first SQLite mutation. Recovery never unlinks a lock pathname, release only unlocks the exact owning descriptor, and consumers fail closed on unprovable ownership while accepting a completed marker despite stale PID reuse. A proven interrupted generation or stale pre-marker numeric lock is carried by the claim and overrides every direct caller to force=True, light=False; watch and Verify refreshes cannot certify a partial DB through an incremental/light run. Genuinely complete legacy DBs and released legacy locks retain normal incremental behavior. complete is published only after SQLite checkpoint/fsync and a durable marker rename. This closes the crash/OOM case where a present-but-partial database returned plausible empty results and caused Compile probes to re-derive answers.
  • PR Replay preserves honest verification context on clean checkouts — every successful replay carries a small deterministic report-generation manifest, so evidence coverage distinguishes “the replay producer ran, but no verification proof exists” from “verification was never considered.” The manifest earns only partial Q7 coverage; it never fabricates tests_run or upgrades the packet to verified.
  • Python 3.14 no longer strips MCP alias annotations at the concurrency boundary — Python 3.14 stopped copying a runtime-assigned __annotations__ mapping through functools.wraps, leaving FastMCP/Pydantic with a synthesized signature but no matching type hints and crashing server import with KeyError: 'symbol'. The guard now preserves a private copy of realized annotations for sync and async tools; direct Pydantic schema generation and FastMCP 3.4 registration are regression-tested without constraining FastMCP to an older major.
  • PR Replay policy assurance is deterministic on fresh checkouts — every successful replay now records the selected current-detector-set policy as a typed not_evaluated decision, explicitly avoiding a fabricated pass/fail result. Constitution, rule, permit, lease, audit-trail, and review decisions remain additive, while Q6 no longer depends on incidental local .roam/ history.
  • MCP receipts and signed run events cannot cross repository roots — the dispatcher snapshots one canonical invocation root and active run before execution, then binds policy, receipt placement, and HMAC linkage to that immutable context even if CWD or ROAM_RUN_ID changes during the call. Foreign, inactive, malformed, hard-linked, symlinked, NTFS-junction, redirected, or concurrently replaced receipt/metadata/event/key paths fail closed. Ledger appends are inode-pinned, and POSIX receipt replacement uses directory handles so a detached-parent race cannot strand evidence outside the verified tree.
  • The complete development/CI dependency graph is vulnerability-clean — the dev-only Pillow floor is now 12.3.0, closing the image-parser advisory wave present in the previous 12.2.0 lock. Pillow remains outside Roam's runtime and publishing dependency graphs.
  • MCP transport/task dependency floor now includes the upstream security fixes — the mcp and development extras require MCP Python SDK 1.28.1 or newer, and the release lock resolves 1.28.1. This closes the authenticated-principal task/session gaps and missing WebSocket Host/Origin validation reported against the previous 1.27.1 lock.
  • Architecture Guardian tolerates transient fresh-runner parser downloads without hiding real failures — the scheduled index build retries roam init --yes up to three times with bounded backoff, then exits non-zero. This seals the observed one-shot tree-sitter-language-pack transport reset while keeping exhausted downloads visible and blocking.
  • Cold parser acquisition is cross-process safe and truthfully documented — the grammar-pack floor is now 1.13.3 with a <1.14 compatibility ceiling. That range serializes cache mutation across processes, publishes manifest/library files atomically, retains one checksum-addressed platform bundle, and lets later grammar loads reuse it locally. Four simultaneous cold-cache indexers pass on both Windows and native Linux. Public, security, privacy, legal, CI, smoke, and air-gap guidance now distinguishes local repository analysis from this one-time public parser-binary retrieval.
  • Hosted deployments can pin a root-owned parser cache without hijacking general XDG state — ROAM_TREE_SITTER_CACHE_DIR accepts only a canonical absolute path and configures the grammar pack before availability or acquisition calls. ROAM_TREE_SITTER_CACHE_SEALED=1 rejects missing grammars before the package's auto-downloading path and disables download retries for cache hits. This lets Prakteon serve an attested read-only parser generation while Claude, Codex, and application caches retain their normal writable locations.
  • Parser availability no longer collapses backend failure into “no findings” — every optional tree-sitter boundary now uses the 1.13.3 networkless has_language() probe to distinguish an unsupported grammar from acquisition, cache, integrity, or runtime failure. Unsupported grammars retain their documented skip or regex fallback; required parser-backend failures remain loud. Deterministic tests pin the new package-specific exception hierarchy and all 40 non-regex Roam language mappings.
  • Transient first-use parser downloads have one bounded retry contract — parser and language acquisition share two short deterministic retries for package DownloadError only. Checksum mismatches, unsupported grammars, runtime failures, and an exhausted download budget remain immediately or ultimately loud; an AST boundary test prevents parser consumers from bypassing the centralized policy.
  • The offline publish wheelhouse now matches the parser runtime floor — the hash-locked release toolchain carries tree-sitter-language-pack 1.13.3 and its reviewed Linux wheel digest, and a regression gate binds that publish input to the package contract. Public installation, network-boundary, troubleshooting, and cancellation copy no longer advertises an unavailable Compile PyPI package, absolute zero-egress behavior, unsupported-grammar reinstalls, or an unresolved account dashboard.
  • The CLI network boundary is now explicit and test-pinned — a canonical inventory documents cold parser acquisition, version --check, metrics-push, GitHub fetch/post paths, external stale-reference probes, keyless Cosign, optional listeners, and project-command inheritance. This replaces the false claim that metrics-push was the only outbound surface and records exact defaults, destinations, and payload classes.
  • MCP-card auto-rotation tests no longer mutate release files — all four write-path tests now copy count inputs, card mirrors, and the SHA-256 pin into a per-test --root shadow. File-based pytest-xdist scheduling can no longer expose a transient test mutation to the real card-hash or mirror readers; a parallel regression asserts that the canonical card is byte-identical before and after the suite.
  • service-report --type due-diligence no longer deadlocks inside clones — report components now cross a literal-argv subprocess boundary, so multiprocessing detectors never spawn from an in-process Click runner. Every component has a 180-second timeout, process-tree cleanup, a 32 MiB output ceiling, duplicate-key rejection, and an explicit failure envelope; the full gather also has one 240-second budget with cleanup reserve, so host contention degrades late evidence explicitly instead of overrunning the caller's five-minute bound. Partial/degraded components are named in both Markdown and JSON instead of collapsing into a successful-looking report. Cost-aware scheduling reserves clones an exclusive slot while overlapping compatible scans, improving the measured warm due-diligence run from 148 seconds serial to 109 seconds (about 26%).
  • Historical transcript mining now fails closed around private filesystem state and resource pressure — .roam, the keyed fingerprint salt, source JSONL files, and the derived snapshot are depth-, row-, directory-, file-, event-, and byte-bounded and checked without following symlinks, junctions, or hard links. Persisted transcript CWD values are normalized, grouped, and HMACed lexically; they never trigger path resolution, existence checks, UNC/SMB access, or automount probes. The default scan keeps the newest 2,000 files per source under a 10,000-file global ceiling, applies global directory/entry budgets across every source, and applies aggregate ceilings of 512 MiB, 1,000,000 JSONL rows, and one 120-second deadline covering discovery plus processing. Selection, traversal, and aggregate-budget truncation are explicit. Snapshot construction serializes incrementally under a 32 MiB / 50,000-event ceiling; duplicate keys, invalid UTF-8, deep JSON, and same-size concurrent rewrites are rejected before any file contributes evidence. Keys are created owner-only with exclusive first-writer semantics and bounded concurrent-read retries. Windows cleanup is bound to the native file identity; platforms without a portable conditional unlink retain the private random tempfile and disclose that state instead of risking deletion of a replacement. Unsafe or changed paths produce a structured error envelope.
  • Savings materialization is bounded and failure-complete — every source log is read from one no-follow descriptor and accepted only when size, identity, timestamps, link count, and owner-only state remain stable through the read. Physical rows and parse time are bounded even when rows are blank or invalid, including a decoder that crosses the deadline mid-row. The rebuild refuses oversized prior databases and sidecars before SQLite access, checks only the bounded current ID set against the prior projection, and caps the installed database at 64 MiB. Its fsynced SQLite artifact is bound to the producer identity, link count, metadata, and SHA-256 digest before all producer handles close. The installer reopens and re-proves that generation while retaining its descriptor through native publication; Windows denies sharing and renames the exact handle with FileRenameInfo, preventing a proved source pathname from being rewritten or replaced before publication. A generation that changes at the final native boundary is moved off the consumer pathname before the exclusive handle is released. Create-only publication remains native no-replace; existing state uses one final destination-generation precheck followed by serialized atomic last-writer-wins replacement, with no pathname-based post-install rollback that could clobber a legitimate later writer. Containment, lock-timeout, SQLite, and operational I/O failures return a canonical JSON error envelope.
  • Compile telemetry and cache warming now preserve their read/write contracts — compile-stats validates owner-only state without repairing ACLs, rejects ambiguous/deep rows with explicit degraded-read counts, and keeps useful KPI verdicts alongside the degradation. Telemetry counts normalized unique prefetched facts, enforces 0..1 classifier confidence and real UTC dates, and opens an existing log once with no-follow/single-link validation before any ACL change or read. compile-cache build streams corpus and Git inputs under byte, line, path, task, and time ceilings and reports every partial input in its standalone verdict.
  • Service-report delivery and engagement persistence are fail-closed — service-report and pr-replay now share one owner-only, no-follow, single-link, root-contained, interprocess-serialized engagement ledger implementation, so a concurrent record from either command cannot be erased by the other's bounded rewrite. History is retained under 2 MiB / 5,000-record ceilings. BSD/macOS descendant-proof limitations propagate into component health, Markdown, and JSON; a requested PDF that cannot be rendered is reported as an artifact failure and is never listed as delivered.
  • Release JSON is unambiguous and bounded at every network/artifact boundary — the manifest, CycloneDX SBOM, and PyPI recovery response now reject duplicate object keys, hard-linked or redirected inputs, concurrent file replacement, and oversized payloads. Every workflow JSON download also has a 16 MiB transport ceiling, preventing last-key-wins interpretation and unbounded disk/parser input before publication.
  • roam capsule --redact-paths no longer leaks the directory tree via cluster labels — the "zero-source" architecture capsule is meant for external review without sharing source, and it correctly hashes every symbol's file path, but clusters[].label (which is derived from a file/directory path) was emitted verbatim — leaking the exact tree the flag exists to anonymize (e.g. workflows/checkout, tests/test_cmd_pr_replay_...). Cluster labels are now hashed with the same per-component scheme as symbol paths under --redact-paths. Surfaced by real dogfooding of the redaction path.
  • roam --json postmortem no longer corrupts its own JSON on stdout — the click.progressbar("Replaying detectors") wrote its label to stdout ahead of the JSON, so roam --json postmortem <range> > out.json produced an unparseable file. The progress chrome now goes to stderr (matching pr-replay), leaving stdout pure JSON.
  • --json / SARIF deliverables no longer leak compile-time SyntaxWarnings — a structured-output run (e.g. service-report --type reachability-triage, a client-facing report) emitted raw interpreter invalid escape sequence '\d' / '\g' / '\ ' lines on stderr, sourced from a dependency's compile() codegen (filename=<unknown>), not from roam's own source (which is SyntaxWarning-clean under the compileall gate). The structured warning handler now drops SyntaxWarning (compile-time, never a user-actionable roam finding) from the customer stream; genuine roam-origin warnings (and all other categories) are still surfaced, and normal non-structured runs are unchanged.
  • A budget-truncated JSON envelope could silently drop its entire payload while summary.partial_success still read false — the same failure shape dfe59667 fixed for attestation, but in the truncator's own disclosure step. roam cycles on any repository whose envelope exceeded the JSON token budget is the concrete case: _drop_fields_to_budget deletes the whole non-preserved cycles list (it's the only payload field the command emits, so there's nothing smaller to drop instead), while summary.cycle_count and summary.verdict kept reporting the true, pre-truncation count. A consumer reading only summary saw a complete, successful result over a payload that had just been discarded, and a consumer defensively reading data.get("cycles", []) could not distinguish "0 cycles found" from "cycles found but discarded". The root cause: _annotate_truncation — the helper budget_truncate_json calls on every truncation, for every command that goes through json_envelope — stamped truncated, budget_tokens, and omitted_low_importance_nodes but never touched partial_success, which defaults to false. This broke an invariant the codebase already documents and tests elsewhere for the sibling --limit cap-disclosure path (summary.partial_success : bool — True iff truncated, see tests/test_w1142_followup_b_cap_disclosure.py). _annotate_truncation now sets partial_success = True whenever it fires, closing the gap for every command that goes through budget_truncate_json (both its callers — json_envelope's own default-cap path and mcp_server.py's explicit --budget path — share this one function), not just cycles. A separate, pre-existing truncation mechanism with the identical disclosure gap — strip_list_payloads / _annotate_summary_disclosure, used by the --detail-aware clusters / dead / deps / health / hotspots / layers / smells commands to elide list payloads in default (non---detail) mode — was found during this audit still emitting truncated: true with partial_success: false on live repositories (confirmed on roam --json health and roam --json layers) and is deliberately NOT touched here: those seven commands already carry dozens of tests encoding a bespoke, per-command partial_success discipline (flip only on failure markers / non-empty warnings_out, never on the clean --detail-elided path), and reconciling that with a blanket "truncated implies partial_success" rule needs its own dedicated pass, not a drive-by inside this fix.
  • summary.truncated: true meant two different things depending on which of two independent mechanisms set it, with no field a consumer could branch on to tell them apart. budget_truncate_json / _annotate_truncation sets it when the JSON token budget forced an involuntary payload drop (summary.partial_success correctly true, per 92a18361 above). strip_list_payloads / _annotate_summary_disclosure — used by the --detail-aware clusters / dead / deps / health / hotspots / layers / smells commands — sets the identical truncated: true when a default (non---detail) invocation intentionally elided its list payloads, with partial_success correctly staying false (confirmed live: roam --json health and roam --json layers both emit truncated: true, partial_success: false). Both states are legitimate and partial_success is right in both cases — but a consumer that only sees truncated: true cannot tell "you didn't ask for detail" from "the budget ate your data" without inferring it from partial_success (itself ambiguous — false could mean "nothing dropped" or "intentionally elided") or from which command it called. Both mechanisms now also stamp summary.truncation_reason: "budget" for the involuntary JSON-budget path, "detail_mode" for the intentional --detail-elision path — a closed two-value enum a consumer can branch on directly, with truncated: true never appearing without one. partial_success semantics are unchanged for all seven --detail-aware commands and their existing tests. Separately, pr-bundle init unconditionally reset summary.partial_success to false after building its envelope, which would have silently re-clobbered a legitimate true set by the same JSON-budget path (e.g. a re-init over an already-large bundle); it now only defaults the flag when the truncator hasn't already raised it.
  • roam attest --sign --format json could emit a packet with no content_hash — no error, exit code 0 — on any repository whose envelope exceeded the JSON token budget. Affected releases: v13.7.0 through v13.9.0. The envelope truncator preserved a fixed set of envelope fields (command, summary, schema, schema_version, version, project, _meta) and dropped every other field in dict insertion order until the payload fit the budget. attestation was not in that set, and it is the first payload field attest declares, so it was deleted ahead of the evidence block queued behind it: on Roam's own repository that meant 1,760 characters of signed contract discarded to make room for a 173,325-character blob which was then discarded anyway. The result is a tamper-evidence failure shaped like a success — roam attest --sign --output packet.json wrote a well-formed packet, printed its usual confirmation, and exited 0, with the seal simply absent. If you hold a JSON attestation packet produced by v13.7.0–v13.9.0 from a repository large enough to truncate, check it for attestation.content_hash and re-issue it if that field is missing. The --format markdown and default text outputs were never affected: both render the attestation directly, before the envelope is assembled, so only JSON artifacts lost the seal. The stale_if freshness contract, introduced in v13.7.1, was lost by the same mechanism over v13.7.1–v13.9.0, as was the bounded agent_contract block on every over-budget envelope of any command. attestation and agent_contract now join the preserved set — both are small, fixed-shape contract blocks that cannot themselves be what exceeds a budget, and agent_contract was already preserved on the sibling strip_list_payloads path — and the remaining fields are now dropped largest-serialised-first, so the field that actually blew the budget goes before smaller fields that merely sat in front of it.
  • A read-only report no longer states a measured zero when it never managed to read the file. Three related defects made local compile/savings telemetry unreadable on the machine that wrote it, and made the resulting nulls indistinguishable from real observations. (1) The UserPromptSubmit hook body spawned its compiler as a bare roam resolved off PATH, so whichever install happened to shadow the active environment did the writing — a stale one writes rows in an older schema and never installs the owner-only state directory. The cold-compile path now resolves through the hook's own interpreter, matching how the hook itself is registered, and the hook-body version is bumped so already-wired installs heal. (2) compile-stats treated one weak property — whether the state directory's ACL is exclusive — as equivalent to the strong property that it is not redirected, and refused the whole read when it was merely inherited (the normal state of any repo predating the owner-only writer, or living under a group-writable parent). Redirection checks — symlink, junction/reparse point, hard link, non-regular file, size bound, and dev/ino identity across the open — remain hard failures; only ACL exclusivity degrades, and it degrades to an explicitly disclosed read state rather than to silence. The agent-facing fact now distinguishes "the log has N rows" from "the log was not read", instead of reporting 0 rows over a populated file. (3) savings exited RUN_FAILED on that same ACL predicate, so "the evidence gate was not met" and "the evidence gate crashed" produced identical output and neither could be recorded. An ACL-only refusal is now an ordinary insufficient_evidence result carrying a per-conjunct breakdown of the seven-way admissibility gate, with each conjunct marked unevaluated rather than failed; redirection-shaped refusals still fail hard. The same breakdown is now the single source of truth for the gate when it does run, so every conjunct reports its observed value and threshold instead of collapsing into one boolean.
  • Telemetry fields whose meaning depends on how a run ended now carry explicit provenance instead of an implicit default. Three surfaces where a mixed or historically-overloaded bucket could be silently averaged as if it were one clean cohort: (1) the compile-telemetry agent_mode=unknown bucket — verified to never mean "the field didn't exist" (it predates every retained row), but it does mix a wider pre-call-site-coverage cohort with a narrower post-coverage one; a documented epoch marker and opt-in split now separate them instead of blending an "unknown" statistic across two different real compositions. (2) the engagement ledger, historically dominated by our own test runs with no field distinguishing them from real usage — new rows now carry an authoritative, non-heuristic source stamp, and legacy rows classify into their own disclosed-heuristic cohort rather than defaulting into "real". (3) the local CLI telemetry ring buffer's exit_code, which a pre-fix build recorded as a hardcoded constant — rows now carry a schema marker so a consumer computing a success/failure rate cannot mistake an always-0 legacy row for a real outcome. In all three cases a row lacking the new marker is classified as pre-marker, never defaulted into the current cohort.
  • changelog.html (the landing-page mirror of CHANGELOG.md, deployed as-is by wrangler pages deploy) could drift and stay committed that way. The render-drift check (scripts/build_changelog_html.py) ran only at push time and in CI — after a stale pair had already been committed — so the fix required a manual follow-up commit whenever anyone noticed (5e8d6360 was exactly that, twice in one session). .githooks/pre-commit now runs the same check at commit time, so a CHANGELOG.md edit that doesn't also re-render the page is blocked before it lands.
  • runs end refused to record a completed status whenever any mirrored event reported partial_success: true, conflating incomplete OUTPUT with a FAILED check. _derive_status_from_recorded_checks treated any partial_success=true event as a failed check, but partial_success was formalised (task #57 / baa37ec9) as an output-completeness signal, not a check verdict — confirmed across cmd_pr_bundle.py (state != complete), cmd_verify.py (execution degraded, never violation count), and cmd_preflight.py (degraded resolution, never risk). A plain pr-bundle init producing a not-yet-fully-assembled bundle document was enough to have the whole run refused; a budget-truncated command hitting the same envelope-truncation partial_success flag would have marked an entire run failed. auto_log now marks every partial_success=true it mirrors from a command's own envelope with partial_success_kind: "output_incomplete"; the status derivation excludes marked events from the failed-check set but still tracks them via RunMeta.partial_output_count, threaded into the signed RunLedgerRoot/v1 predicate, so a verifier sees "completed, derived, AND N checks returned partial output" together rather than losing the signal. A raw/manual partial_success=true with no marker is still an explicit recorded failure and still refuses completed — preserving the original protection (closed hole 12c8b34d).
